tagline: A limestone valley enclosed by Garden Mountain, with a church shared across denominations.
intro: Burke's Garden is an upland valley in Virginia's Tazewell County, enclosed by Garden Mountain. Its bowl-like shape resembles a crater on maps, but the valley formed from an uplifted dome, with limestone more easily eroded than the sandstone of the surrounding ridges.

Away from major river transportation corridors, the valley remained relatively isolated. In the late nineteenth century, Vanderbilt family agents approached farmers to buy land for an estate. The farmers declined to sell; the family built Biltmore near Asheville instead.
VA 623 crosses the Appalachian Trail at Garden Mountain. Within Burke's Garden, Central Lutheran Church began as a church for several denominations. Wolf Creek drains the valley toward the northeast.

moments.title: Garden Mountain
moments.text: The Appalachian Trail follows the ridge of Garden Mountain, with views into Burke's Garden, and crosses VA 623. The mountain was part of the ancient dome whose erosion left the enclosed valley. Along the ridge, the trail passes through a large stand of old-growth forest, with occasional glimpses of the valley. Garden Mountain Wilderness borders VA 623 on its eastern side; its elevations range from 2,500 feet at Lick Creek to 4,080 feet at the mountain crest. The wilderness surrounds the headwaters of Lick Creek, with steep-sided drainages on the mountain’s lower slopes.

moments.title: Burke's Garden
moments.text: The entire valley forms the Burke's Garden Rural Historic District on the National Register of Historic Places. German immigrants settled here in the late eighteenth century. Amish families arrived in the 1990s, then left when they could not acquire enough land or attract enough families for a viable community. Amish residents have since returned and operate their own school at the Burkes Garden School and Community Center. The community occupies land once covered by an ancient sea, and Wolf Creek carries its drainage toward the New River.

moments.title: Central Lutheran Church
moments.text: Central Lutheran Church is a plain rectangular frame building with a steep gable roof, built in 1875. It began as a union church serving several denominations. When members learned that the church had joined the Lutheran denomination, most left and established Methodist and Presbyterian churches. The cemetery dates to 1827 and contains sandstone Germanic gravestones. The cemetery predates the present frame church; its gravestones accompany a congregation that began by sharing its place of worship. The church now serves the Lutheran denomination exclusively, and the church and cemetery entered the National Register of Historic Places in 1979.
moments.notice: The cemetery contains sandstone Germanic gravestones.
